title: Trace the J-curve

predict.q: The currency depreciates by 10% in quarter 0. Elasticities rise from a sum of 0.7 to 1.5 over two years. What happens to the trade balance over the next 8 quarters?

options.s: It improves at once and keeps improving.
options.fb: In the short run contracts and habits keep volumes nearly fixed while import prices jump.
The balance starts at −2.6 and climbs to +5.7 by quarter 8 as the elasticity sum passes 1: the J-curve.
True only if the elasticity sum stays below 1; here it rises to 1.5.

options.s: It does not change, because the depreciation cancels out.
options.fb: A depreciation changes relative prices; volumes and the import bill both respond.

task: Move the quarter slider from 0 to 8 and watch the balance trace its path. Then set the long-run elasticity sum to 0.9 and watch again.

target.do: Move the quarter slider to 8 (long-run sum 1.5), then press Check.

takeaway: The balance worsens while elasticities are low, and improves only once their sum passes 1.
